appBuilderComponents.name: Commerce Integration Starter Kit
appBuilderComponents.description: Adobe's Commerce integration starter kit (App Management generation): scaffolding for bidirectional product, customer, order and stock sync, declared in app.commerce.config.ts and installed into Commerce through the app's own generated install API

appBuilderComponents.name: Custom Integration
appBuilderComponents.description: A minimal custom integration to build out with AI — starts from a working deploy, then grows into whatever your demo needs

appBuilderComponents.name: ERP
appBuilderComponents.description: A stand-in ERP the integration talks to: products, business partners, contract prices and sales orders, every record resettable, with its own screen. Comes with the ERP integration and goes with it.

appBuilderComponents.name: ERP Integration

setupSteps.label: Confirmed status
setupSteps.title: Create the "Confirmed in ERP" order status
setupSteps.why: Without it, an order the ERP confirmed looks the same as one it never saw in the Orders grid.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Settings > Order Status: create erp_confirmed, assign it to Pending (not as default), then pick it for "Order status when the ERP confirms" on the integration's Mapping tab.
setupSteps.then: Assign it to Pending (not as default), then pick it on the integration's Mapping tab.

setupSteps.label: Shared catalogs
setupSteps.title: Give each priced company its own shared catalog
setupSteps.why: The ERP publishes a company's prices into that company's shared catalog; companies sharing one would share prices.
setupSteps.where: Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Add Shared Catalog, then Assign Companies.
setupSteps.then: Assign the company under Assign Companies.

setupSteps.label: Price scope
setupSteps.title: Set the catalog price scope to Website
setupSteps.why: The ERP publishes a company's prices per website; at the default scope, Global, every site would show the same prices. No API sets this.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Price > Catalog Price Scope: set to Website, Save Config. Catalog > Shared Catalogs > Set Pricing and Structure then shows a Website chooser above the prices.

setupSteps.label: ERP warehouse
setupSteps.title: Give the ERP a warehouse of its own, and a stock that sells it
setupSteps.why: The ERP keeps stock per Commerce source; the Default Stock can hold only the Default Source, so the website needs a stock of its own.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Inventory > Sources > Add New Source (for example Northwind Warehouse); Stores > Inventory > Stocks > Add New Stock with the website as its sales channel and the new source assigned; then move the website's products' quantities to the new source (Catalog > Products > Actions > Move stock between the ERP's warehouses) and save each product once, so the storefront's catalog reads the new stock.
setupSteps.then: Add a stock for the website with that source, move the products' quantities to it, and save each product once.

setupSteps.label: Product attributes
setupSteps.title: Create the erp_owner and brand product attributes
setupSteps.why: Each product goes to the ERP its erp_owner names (the ERP's list id: its name in lower case without the word ERP — Justrite ERP is justrite); brand is what buyers filter on.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Attributes > Product > Add New Attribute: erp_owner as a Text Field (a Dropdown sends a number, not the id) and brand; then Stores > Attributes > Attribute Set to add both to the set. Set both on the products you sell.
setupSteps.then: erp_owner is a Text Field; add both to the attribute set and set them on every product.

setupSteps.label: Partially Held status
setupSteps.title: Create the "Partially Held" order status
setupSteps.why: When one ERP holds its part of an order and another carries on, the order says so; without it the integration writes only a note.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Settings > Order Status: create partially_held (label Partially Held), then assign it to Processing and to Pending (not as default, not visible on the storefront).
setupSteps.then: Assign it to Processing and Pending (not as default, not visible on the storefront).

setupSteps.label: Payment on Account
setupSteps.title: Switch on Payment on Account for the website
setupSteps.why: Company buyers pay against the company's credit line, which the ERP credit story needs.
setupSteps.where: Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods > Payment on Account, at the website's scope: untick Use Default beside Enabled, set Enabled to Yes, Save Config.
setupSteps.then: At the website's scope, untick Use Default first, then Save Config.

appBuilderComponents.description: Adobe Commerce and an ERP, on the Commerce integration starter kit: orders get an ERP number, price, stock and order-status changes in the ERP land in Commerce, contract prices apply in the cart, and a screen inside the Commerce Admin shows it all. Comes with its own ERP.
